clue.text: Sebastian, explorer-sailor in his hammock

indicators.note: the seaman is placed inside the swinging bed, signalled by in here

parts.note: a cot is a hanging bed on board ship, like a hammock
AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor named Sebastian lies in his hammock.
explanation.definitionFit: Sebastian Cabot was a Venetian-born navigator who sailed under the English and Spanish crowns.

clue.text: Building-society worker dressed in crisp lace

indicators.note: the worker is clothed by the other word, so it sits inside it

parts.note: crisp weather is cold, chilly
an ant is a worker in a colony, a society that builds its nest

explanation.surface: A clerk from a building society wears crisp lace clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building-society' suggests a British mortgage lender (a savings bank), but it means an ant colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Chantilly is a fine bobbin lace named after the French town where it was made.

clue.text: Fetch Bill inside for tonic

indicators.note: the bill goes within the word for fetch

parts.note: to fetch is to bring
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Fetch the bill and pour a tonic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bracing is invigorating, just as a tonic refreshes.

clue.text: Empty, picking up contract

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to contract is to draw together, so to meet

explanation.surface: An empty office is picking up a new contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Teem in an older sense means to pour out or drain a vessel.

clue.text: Number of Elgar's overture announced

indicators.note: the drug's name is said aloud, giving the title's sound

parts.note: a number is something that numbs, like the anaesthetic cocaine

explanation.surface: A number from an Elgar overture is announced at a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as a numeral or piece, but it is a numbing agent. Elgar's 'In London Town' overture is named after a fabled land of plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgar wrote a concert overture titled after the mythical land of luxury, a nickname for London.

clue.text: One who gets heart-throbs into the charts?

definitions.text: One who gets heart-throbs into the charts?

parts.words: One who gets heart-throbs into the charts?
parts.note: seems to be a pop promoter of idols, but means a technician recording heartbeats on a chart

explanation.surface: A music manager makes teen idols hit the top of the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: A technician who records the heart's beats as traces on paper charts.

clue.text: Perhaps easy to hide church recess

indicators.note: the recess is concealed within the run of the words before it

explanation.surface: A church alcove is perhaps an easy place to hide.
explanation.definitionFit: A semicircular vaulted recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Furze divine for a druids meeting

parts.note: furze is another name for the shrub gorse
a divine is a clergyman, here a DD, Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: A druid divines among the furze bushes at a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh assembly of bards and druids held at an eisteddfod.

clue.text: First lady right to turn out

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: The First Lady was right to turn out for the event.
explanation.definitionFit: To evert is to turn outwards or inside out.

clue.text: Status of players in a RU team turning out?

indicators.note: the letters are turned out into a new order

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union, taken as letters

explanation.surface: Players in a rugby union side turn out without being paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpaid players hold non-professional standing, as rugby union did until 1995.

clue.text: Pain suffered by athletes gathering tacks?

definitions.meaning: a side pain got while running
a simple sewing tack used to gather fabric

explanation.surface: Athletes suffer pain as they gather on the track.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner's side cramp and a simple in-and-out sewing technique used for gathering both bear this name.

clue.text: Game-forest book

definitions.meaning: an area of land kept for wildlife
to book is to arrange a place in advance

explanation.surface: A book about a forest full of game.
explanation.definitionFit: A wildlife park is so named, and to book a table is to secure it ahead.

clue.text: Outing from Turkey on a vehicle-one penny!

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle registration code for Turkey
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An outing from Turkey on a coach costs just one penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is an excursion or journey out.

clue.text: What a caper, putting worker in charge!

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: An exclamation at the folly of promoting a mere worker to the boss's role.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a playful or grotesque prank or caper.

clue.text: Fellow in silly yarn

indicators.note: the fellow goes inside the word for silly

parts.note: wet is British slang for feeble or silly

explanation.surface: A man spins a silly tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' suggests a story, but here it is woven thread.
explanation.definitionFit: The weft is the crosswise thread woven through the warp.

clue.text: Handsome fiddle putting up pub game

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up lifts the word so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: darts is the classic British pub game

explanation.surface: A handsome violin is put up as a prize in a pub game.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stradivarius, the costly violin made by Antonio Stradivari.

clue.text: Mind it leaving Britain?

indicators.note: the two letters depart from the country's name

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Would you mind it if they left Britain?
explanation.definitionFit: The brain is the seat of thought, the intellect.

clue.text: Felt insignificant at first, like Jack Dawkins

indicators.note: the word for insignificant comes before the word for felt

parts.note: something light is trivial or insignificant
to finger something is to feel it

explanation.surface: Someone felt small at first, like a character from Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Dawkins is the Artful Dodger, the pickpocket in Dickens's Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Artful Dodger was a deft pickpocket, given to thieving.

clue.text: Take-home bread-wrapper?

parts.note: bread is slang for money, so the wrapper holds the wages brought home

explanation.surface: A bag for carrying a loaf home.
explanation.definitionFit: The envelope holding a worker's weekly wages.

clue.text: Fickleness of variety-skill?

parts.note: change brings variety
ability is skill

explanation.surface: A variety performer's skill is unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fickle means being inconstant, liable to alter.

clue.text: Can not even reduce the mess

parts.note: can not contracts to can't

indicators.note: the word is shortened by losing a letter, as poets elide it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Even reducing can't clear the mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduce' cuts EVEN to EEN, the poetic e'en.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a dining hall, as a military mess is.

clue.text: Men fail, somehow, to excite passion

indicators.note: the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: Men somehow fail to arouse passion.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflame is to stir up strong feelings.

clue.text: Long piece of wood

explanation.surface: A long piece of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn for something, and timber from a conifer.

clue.text: Troublesome dyspepsia said to have left the chronicler

indicators.note: the letters are troubled into a new order

parts.note: these letters are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: The diarist's indigestion is said to have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of SAID from DYSPEPSIA and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys kept the famous diary of 1660s London.

clue.text: Sort of feet to evoke wanderlust?

definitions.text: Sort of feet to evoke wanderlust?

parts.words: Sort of feet to evoke wanderlust?
parts.note: an idiom for restlessness, the urge to travel

explanation.surface: Restless feet yearn to wander.
explanation.definitionFit: Having itchy feet means feeling a restless urge to travel.

clue.text: Cricket-side taking on a builder of earthworks

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A cricket team takes on a builder of earthworks.
explanation.definitionFit: King Offa of Mercia had the great dyke built along the Welsh border.

clue.text: Girl who received a rave review

indicators.note: the letters are reviewed, looked at anew, in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A girl got a rave review.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name.

clue.text: Silver, topped with tin, can be a problem

indicators.note: in a down clue, the tin is placed on top of the silver

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A silver item topped with tin can cause a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is an unexpected difficulty or hitch.

clue.text: Contemporary stage?

definitions.meaning: to put on, as a play

explanation.surface: A modern stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Current or existing now, and to put on a show.

clue.text: Search for doctor's bag in station

indicators.note: the bag is put inside the word for station

parts.note: rank is one's station in life
a sac is a bag-like part of the body, in medical terms

explanation.surface: Searching for the doctor's bag in the station.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack is to search thoroughly and roughly.

clue.text: One suffering heat-burns?

indicators.note: the letters suffer damage and come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone suffering burns from the heat.
explanation.definitionFit: A person lying out in the sun.

clue.text: Welcome cry in Scotland

definitions.meaning: a Scots word meaning to weep

explanation.surface: A Scottish greeting with tears.
explanation.definitionFit: To welcome someone, and to weep in Scots dialect.
